chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ghazafar from Uqbah ibn Yunus from Abdullah ibn Sharik, in his hadith—which we have abridged—

He said: Husain (peace be upon him) passed by a group of the Umayyads while they were sitting in the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'By Allah, the world will not pass away until Allah sends from me a man who will kill from you one thousand, and with the thousand another thousand, and with the thousand another thousand.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, these are the sons of so-and-so; they do not reach this number.' He said: 'Woe to you! At that time, a man will have from his loins so-and-so many men, and their chief will be from themselves.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husain (peace be upon him) predict about the number of enemies the Mahdi would defeat?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Husain (a.s.) foretells the rise of the Mahdi from his progeny, emphasizing a miraculous multiplication of his descendants to overcome the Umayyads. The dialogue highlights the concept of 'Mawlā al-Qawm min anfusihim' (the leader is one of them), underscoring the Mahdi's authentic lineage and leadership within the expanded family of Husain. This prediction serves as a key proof for the Mahdi's origin in Shia eschatology, linking the victory of the Ahl al-Bayt to divine promise and lineage.
